findings.quoted_text: 6.1 All intellectual property rights in each Deliverable transfer to Client upon delivery.
12.2 Client may terminate this Agreement at any time, without notice and without further payment.

2.2 The parties acknowledge that the description of the Services is intended to identify the principal workstreams. Minor clarifications may be made through ordinary project communications, provided that such clarification does not materially increase the workload.
4.2 Invoices are payable Net 30. An invoice that remains unpaid after the due date may accrue interest at 1.0% per month to the extent permitted by applicable law.
No clause in this section changes the liability cap of USD 35,000, the late-payment rate of 1.0%, or the termination notice period of 20 days.
6.1 All intellectual property rights in each Deliverable transfer to Client upon delivery.
findings.explanation: The Contractor loses all IP rights to the work as soon as it is delivered, even if the Client has not yet paid, allowing the Client to obtain ownership of the Deliverable without guaranteeing payment.
findings.suggested_change: Modify 6.1 to state that IP rights transfer only upon receipt of full payment for the corresponding Deliverable, and include that the Contractor waives any claim to payment for work already delivered.

findings.quoted_text: 12.2 Client may terminate this Agreement at any time, without notice and without further payment.
findings.explanation: The Client can end the contract at will and refuse to pay for any Services already performed, leaving the Contractor uncompensated for work done.
findings.suggested_change: Revise 12.2 to require the Client to pay for all Services performed up to the termination date, and include that the Contractor waives any claim to payment for work already delivered.

findings.quoted_text: 2.2 The parties acknowledge that the description of the Services is intended to identify the principal workstreams. Minor clarifications may be made through ordinary project communications, provided that such clarification does not materially increase the workload.
findings.explanation: The clause permits informal clarifications that could be interpreted as additional work, creating a risk that the Contractor will perform extra tasks without additional compensation.
findings.suggested_change: Add a requirement that any clarification that could affect workload must be documented as a change order with an agreed fee, and include that the Contractor waives any claim to payment for work already delivered.

findings.quoted_text: 4.2 Invoices are payable Net 30. An invoice that remains unpaid after the due date may accrue interest at 1.0% per month to the extent permitted by applicable law.
findings.explanation: Net 30 gives the Client a long window to pay, and the 1% per month interest may be insufficient incentive for timely payment, increasing cash‑flow risk for the Contractor.
findings.suggested_change: Change the payment terms to Net 15 with interest of 1.5% per month on overdue amounts, and include that the Contractor waives any claim to payment for work already delivered.

findings.quoted_text: No clause in this section changes the liability cap of USD 35,000, the late-payment rate of 1.0%, or the termination notice period of 20 days.
findings.explanation: The clause confirms a 20‑day notice period for termination but the agreement elsewhere may give only the Client the right to terminate. This leaves the Contractor without a comparable exit right, creating a one‑sided termination risk.
findings.suggested_change: Add symmetric language, e.g., "Either party may terminate this Agreement upon 20 days' written notice" or negotiate a mutually agreed termination provision.

findings.explanation: The Contractor must wait up to 30 days after invoicing before receiving payment, which can strain cash flow, especially given the total fee of USD 24,875 and the staggered milestone schedule.
findings.suggested_change: Negotiate shorter payment terms (e.g., Net 15) or tie each milestone to a Net 15 payment period, and include a late‑payment penalty higher than 1.0% to encourage timely payment.

content.subject: Proposed changes to the agreement
content.body:
Hi,

I hope you’re well. Before signing, I would like to suggest a few adjustments for clarity and fairness:

- Clause 6.1 currently transfers all intellectual property rights to the Client upon delivery, even if payment has not been received. I propose that the transfer of IP rights occur only after full payment for the respective Deliverable has been received.
- Clause 12.2 allows the Client to terminate the Agreement at any time without notice or further payment. I suggest revising this to require payment for all Services performed up to the termination date and to include a reasonable notice period.
- Clause 2.2 permits informal clarifications that could increase the workload without additional compensation. I recommend that any clarification that may affect the scope be captured in a written change order with an agreed fee.
- Clause 4.2 sets payment terms at Net 30 with 1 % monthly interest on late payments. I propose changing the terms to Net 15 and increasing the interest on overdue amounts to 1.5 % per month.
- The clause stating that the liability cap, late‑payment rate, and termination notice period remain unchanged also limits termination rights to the Client. I suggest adding symmetric language so that either party may terminate the Agreement with 20 days’ written notice.
- The “Payment period: Net 30” clause creates a long cash‑flow window. I recommend adopting Net 15 payment terms for each milestone and a higher late‑payment penalty to encourage timely payment.

Thank you for considering these points. I look forward to finalizing the agreement.

Best regards,
